headline: Rajya Sabha Passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by Voice Vote
fullText:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

Rajya Sabha Passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by Voice Vote

Bill Covers Entire Spectrum of Unfair Means Beyond Question Paper Leaks: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Highlights Reforms Already Implemented to Make Public Examinations More Transparent, Efficient and Candidate-Friendly

Government committed to safeguarding interests of students and youth through robust legal framework and comprehensive examination reforms

30 JUL 2026 10:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Rajya Sabha today passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, as passed by the Lok Sabha, by voice vote. Replying to the discussion on the Bill, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the amendments would further strengthen the legal framework for preventing unfair means in public examinations while safeguarding the interests of students and youth.

The Minister said the Government is committed to ensuring that public examinations remain transparent, credible and merit-based so that the sincere efforts of students are protected. Emphasising that the legislation is not confined to question paper leaks alone, he said the Bill seeks to prevent the entire spectrum of unfair means in public examinations. He said the law comprehensively addresses offences ranging from leakage of question papers and answer keys, tampering with answer sheets and computer systems, manipulation of examination processes, creation of fake websites and admit cards, to organised attempts to facilitate unfair means in examinations. These provisions, he said, reflect the comprehensive nature of the legislation in addressing diverse forms of examination-related malpractice.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government had brought the Amendment Bill with humility and an open mind, welcoming constructive suggestions from Members to further strengthen the legislation. He said the issue of unfair means in public examinations concerns every parent, every family and every citizen of the country, as it directly impacts the aspirations of students and the nation's future human resource.

Highlighting the Government's efforts to strengthen the education ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the National Education Policy 2020 has brought transformational reforms by providing greater academic flexibility and expanding opportunities for students. He informed the House that the number of universities in the country has increased from 760 to 1,293, while higher education institutions have grown from 51,534 to 64,896.

Referring to reforms in medical education, the Minister said the number of AIIMS has increased from seven to twenty-two, medical colleges from 387 to 844, undergraduate medical seats from 51,300 to 1.39 lakh and postgraduate medical seats from 31,000 to 86,300, making quality medical education more accessible and affordable.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the Government's initiatives for expanding educational opportunities and employment. He said 400 Eklavya Model Residential Schools are now functional across the country. Referring to employment generation, he said Government appointments increased from 7.22 lakh during 2004–2014 to 10.96 lakh during 2014–2024. He also noted that the Government has cleared backlog vacancies and undertaken special promotion drives to improve career progression in public service.

The Minister said the Government has also encouraged entrepreneurship among youth through the Startup India initiative. He informed the House that the number of recognised startups has increased from around 350–400 at the launch of the initiative to nearly 2.4 lakh today, making India the world's third-largest startup ecosystem. He also noted significant growth in innovation, research and intellectual property generation, with India now ranking among the leading countries in PhD output and patent filings.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 covers examinations conducted by major recruitment agencies, including the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) and the National Testing Agency (NTA). Highlighting reforms already introduced in examination systems, he said interviews have been abolished for specified government recruitments, online application systems and candidate-friendly examination processes have been introduced, provisional answer keys have enhanced transparency and cyber security measures have been strengthened. He further informed the House that the average recruitment cycle in the Staff Selection Commission has been reduced from nine months and eight days to eight months and twenty-four days. Referring to the Pratibha Setu initiative, he said the portal has been created to connect meritorious civil services candidates with prospective employers and that 335 private companies have already registered on the platform.

The Minister informed the House that implementation of the recommendations of the high-level expert committee constituted to strengthen the public examination ecosystem is progressing steadily. He said 35 of the committee's 46 recommendations have already been implemented, including Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, AI-enabled face authentication, multi-layer frisking, CCTV surveillance, signal jammers, State and district coordination committees, grievance redressal mechanisms and restructuring of the National Testing Agency.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said strengthening the integrity of public examinations requires the collective participation of Government, educational institutions, parents, students and society at large. Reiterating that the Government remains open to constructive suggestions from all stakeholders, he said the Government will continue to strengthen the public examination system to ensure that it remains fair, transparent, credible and free from unfair means while safeguarding the aspirations of millions of students and job aspirants.

(Release ID: 2292127)
summaryText:

- **Examination reforms**:

  - Online application systems and candidate‑friendly processes introduced.

headline: Department of Telecommunications Signs MoU with Government of Madhya Pradesh for Establishment of Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Department of Telecommunications Signs MoU with Government of Madhya Pradesh for Establishment of Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior

TMZ to emerge as India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone; ₹493 crore Central Government support for Phase-I infrastructure

India's First Telecom Manufacturing Zone to Advance Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat

We are partners, facilitators, not government: Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

India Must Transition from Being a Telecom Service Provider to a Telecom Product Manufacturer; the Telecom Manufacturing Zone Will Drive This Transformation: Shri Scindia

We are partners and Facilitators for the Investment Community: Union Minister of Communications

30 JUL 2026 9:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the establishment of a Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the presence of Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. The MoU marks a significant milestone in strengthening India’s domestic telecom manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector.

The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is envisaged as an integrated 350-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster, designed to provide world-class infrastructure and a conducive ecosystem for telecom and electronics manufacturing, research and development, innovation and allied activities. The initiative is aimed at positioning Gwalior as a premier industrial and technology hub in Central India and strengthening India’s position as a global telecom manufacturing and innovation hub.

The signing of the MoU will pave the way for the establishment of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for the TMZ, with 51 per cent equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49 per cent from the Department of Telecommunications.

The Central Government is providing 100 per cent funding support for Phase-I, with an allocation of ₹493 crore for development of core infrastructure. The Government of Madhya Pradesh, in turn, has extended significant support for the project, including approximately 170 acres of land free of cost.

Under the special policy package extended by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, 100 acres in the SADA region and 70 acres in the Gwalior IT Park have been allocated free of cost, with a combined value of approximately ₹596 crore. Additional land will be made available at a nominal premium of ₹1 and a fixed lease rent of ₹1 per square metre per annum for 30 years. Units established in the TMZ will also benefit from reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges, power tariff rebates and other fiscal incentives.

The policy package provides substantial support to investors and manufacturers, including 50 per cent capital subsidy on Eligible Fixed Capital Investment (EFCI), subject to a maximum of ₹200 crore, along with employment generation assistance of ₹5,000 per month per employee for five years for eligible mega projects. Skill development support of up to ₹13,000 per new employee will also be available, subject to applicable conditions.

To promote exports, eligible units will receive a 50 per cent freight subsidy on finished goods transported to seaports or air cargo facilities, subject to prescribed limits. The package also provides incentives for research and development, including reimbursement support for standalone R&D units and 100 per cent reimbursement of expenses incurred for filing patents, copyrights and trademarks, within specified limits.

The TMZ is expected to serve as a major investment catalyst, with initial commitments of approximately ₹5,000 crore for Phase-I and projected total investments of ₹12,000–15,000 crore over time. The project is expected to generate approximately 14,000 direct skilled jobs, including around 3,500 jobs in Phase-I, besides creating tens of thousands of indirect employment opportunities.

Leading telecom and electronics companies, including Dixon Technologies, HFCL, Tejas Networks, VVDN and Syrma SGS, are among the industry players anchoring the proposed zone.

The TMZ is envisaged to bring together the entire telecom value chain, ranging from mobile devices and optical fibre to advanced semiconductor technologies and next-generation 5G/6G research and development. Dedicated R&D centres, common testing laboratories and certification facilities will support the development and validation of indigenous telecom technologies and products in accordance with global standards.

The initiative will also create synergies with key national programmes, including the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) and Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF). By strengthening domestic manufacturing of critical telecom equipment such as routers, antennas, optical fibre and chips, the TMZ will contribute towards reducing import dependence, promoting exports, strengthening domestic supply chains and enhancing telecom security.

Expressing his view, Shri Jyotiraditya Madhavrao Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region said, “India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone will be established in Gwalior, the heart of the country, and will accelerate Madhya Pradesh’s growth trajectory.” He said this is a historic milestone in realizing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, Digital India and Viksit Bharat 2047 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The project will strengthen India’s position on the global telecom manufacturing map. He added that under the leadership of Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, Madhya Pradesh is progressing rapidly towards development and self-reliance, and the Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a clear reflection of that vision.

The Union Minister also added, “India must now move beyond being a telecom service provider to becoming a telecom manufacturer, and that building a strong indigenous ecosystem is essential to achieving this goal. The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a major step in that direction.”

Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister, Madhya Pradesh highlighted the significance of TMZ in his state and said, “ The Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is the outcome of Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s sustained efforts and visionary leadership.” He highlighted the Shri Scindia family’s historic contribution to the development of Gwalior and said the project represents another important chapter in that journey.

The Chief Minister expressed confidence that the Telecom Manufacturing Zone would shape not only the industrial and technological future of Madhya Pradesh but also of the country. “What cannot be found anywhere else in India will now be available in Madhya Pradesh,” he said, adding that Gwalior is set to become a national hub for electronics and telecom manufacturing, attracting significant investment, employment and technological innovation.

Speaking on the development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development said, “It is a historic day for both Department of Telecommunications and Government of Madhya Pradesh for establishing first of its kind similar to a SEZ where you put everything from end to end whether it is research, manpower, design, testing and manufacturing in one area. We want to design, patents and intellectual property rights and globally competitive products and this manufacturing zone will help in achieving that.”

Following the MoU signing, an Investor Roundtable was held under the joint chairmanship of Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. The roundtable brought together representatives of telecom manufacturers and industry stakeholders from across the country to discuss investment opportunities, industry requirements and the potential of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior to strengthen India’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem. Various industry leaders applauded the initiative of the both Central and state governments and termed as a historic and best in the world offer and opportunity for the telecom manufacturers and stakeholders. At the end of the roundtable, a total of INR 3,500 crore investment and 14,000 job opportunities were committed by the industry towards the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

The establishment of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior represents a strategic step towards creating a globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem in India. By integrating manufacturing, R&D, common infrastructure, policy support and industry participation, the TMZ is expected to drive investments, create high-quality employment, boost exports, promote indigenous innovation and strengthen India’s telecom supply chain.

The signing of the MoU between the Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh marks the beginning of a new chapter in India’s journey towards becoming a global hub for telecom manufacturing and innovation.

A historic chapter for #AatmanirbharBharat 🇮🇳

A golden moment for Bharat, and a deeply personal one for me, as we sign the MoU between @DoT_India, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) to be set up in Gwalior, in the august… pic.twitter.com/yzCoST2EYC

— Jyotiraditya M. Scindia (@JM_Scindia) July 30, 2026

headline: Government Continues Educational Support for OBC Students Through Scholarships and Free Coaching Schemes
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Continues Educational Support for OBC Students Through Scholarships and Free Coaching Schemes

Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class Education and Free Coaching Schemes Ensuring Greater Access to Quality Education for OBC Students Across the Country

30 JUL 2026 9:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen educational opportunities for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) through a comprehensive set of scholarship and coaching schemes aimed at improving access to quality education and enhancing their participation in higher education and competitive examinations. These initiatives are designed to provide financial assistance, academic support and equal opportunities to students from socially and educationally disadvantaged communities.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM, SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI, SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL, SHRI NILESH DNYANDEV LANKE, DR. SHIVAJI BANDAPPA KALGE in the Lok Sabha.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing a number of welfare schemes for OBC students, including the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs & Others, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs & Others, Top Class Education in Schools for OBCs & Others, Top Class Education in Colleges for OBCs & Others, and the Free Coaching Scheme for Scheduled Castes (SCs), OBCs and beneficiaries of the PM CARES Children Scheme.

Financial assistance under the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes is released to States and Union Territories based on Notional Allocation, enabling them to extend scholarship benefits to eligible students. Under the Top Class Education Schemes and the Free Coaching Scheme, financial assistance is transferred directly to eligible beneficiaries through the Aadhaar-enabled Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism, ensuring transparency and timely disbursal of benefits.

The Central Sector Scheme of Free Coaching seeks to enhance the competitiveness of students from disadvantaged communities by providing quality coaching for various competitive examinations conducted for recruitment to Government and private sector jobs, as well as for admission to reputed technical and professional higher educational institutions.

The scheme is currently being implemented through Dr. Ambedkar Centres of Excellence (DACE) established in 19 empanelled Central Universities, with 100 coaching seats earmarked in each university. In Maharashtra, Mahatma Gandhi Hindi Antarrashtriya Vishwavidyalaya, Wardha, has been empanelled under the scheme. In Madhya Pradesh, the scheme is being implemented through Indira Gandhi National Tribal University, Amarkantak, and Dr. Harisingh Gour Vishwavidyalaya, Sagar. At present, there is no empanelled Central University under the scheme in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

The Minister further informed that the revision of scholarship and coaching assistance under these schemes is undertaken periodically in consultation with all concerned stakeholders, ensuring that the schemes remain responsive to the educational needs of students while supporting the Government's vision of inclusive and equitable development.

The Government reiterated its commitment to ensuring that no deserving student is deprived of educational opportunities due to financial constraints. Through sustained investments in scholarships, quality coaching and direct financial assistance, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower OBC students with the knowledge, skills and opportunities required to participate effectively in the nation's social and economic progress.

PR-044- TAR/KV/GA

(Release ID: 2292099)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reaffirmed its commitment to expanding educational opportunities for OBC students by continuing a suite of scholarship and free‑coaching schemes that provide financial aid, academic support, and transparent benefit delivery through direct benefit transfer mechanisms.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Pre‑Matric and Post‑Matric scholarships are disbursed to states and Union Territories based on Notional Allocation.  
- Top Class Education and Free Coaching Scheme benefits are transferred directly to beneficiaries via Aadhaar‑enabled Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).  
- The Free Coaching Scheme targets competitive examinations for government and private sector jobs and admission to technical institutions.

- No DACE has been empanelled in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.  
- Scholarship and coaching assistance are periodically revised in consultation with stakeholders to align with student needs.  
- The Ministry’s initiatives involve officials Shri B. L. Verma and several nominated members of Parliament.

headline: Swachhata Pakhwada 2026: Ministry of MSME Reinforces Commitment to Cleanliness, Sustainability and Jan Bhagidari
fullText:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

Swachhata Pakhwada 2026: Ministry of MSME Reinforces Commitment to Cleanliness, Sustainability and Jan Bhagidari

Ministry of MSME Drives Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 with Tree Plantation Drives, Cleanliness Pledges, and Sustainable Practices Across India

30 JUL 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is observing Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16th to 31st July 2026 through a broad range of activities that underscore its commitment to environmental sustainability and the vision of Swachh Bharat. Organised across the Ministry's offices, attached and subordinate organisations, autonomous bodies and field formations, the campaign promotes waste reduction, resource conservation, tree plantation, cleanliness, eco-friendly practices and environmental awareness, while encouraging employees and stakeholders to adopt sustainable habits and contribute to building a cleaner, greener and more resilient India.

Shri Jitan Ram Majhi, Union Minister for MSME, Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME, and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME) participated in a plantation drive under the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative. The activity reflected the Ministry's commitment to promoting environmental conservation alongside the objectives of Swachhata Pakhwada, while reinforcing the message that cleanliness and a green environment go hand in hand. The plantation drive also encouraged greater environmental consciousness and public participation, highlighting the importance of collective efforts towards building a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

The campaign gathered significant momentum with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME). Officers and employees of the Ministry, along with officials from its attached and subordinate organisations, participated in the pledge-taking ceremony, reaffirming their collective resolve to uphold the ideals of cleanliness and contribute meaningfully to the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

Further strengthening the Swachhata Pakhwada campaign, Shri Vinamra Mishra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of MSME, addressed officers and representatives of the Ministry's attached organisations, subordinate offices and field formations during a 'Swachhata Talk' organised as part of the Pakhwada. Emphasising that cleanliness is not merely a periodic campaign but a shared civic responsibility, he urged all organisations to actively participate in the Swachhata Pakhwada by organising meaningful cleanliness drives, awareness programmes and sustainable initiatives within their offices as well as in the surrounding communities.

Throughout the Pakhwada, the Ministry is encouraging its attached, subordinate and field offices across the country to undertake a diverse range of activities, including cleanliness drives, plantation programmes, public awareness campaigns, record management and disposal, waste segregation, reduction of single-use plastics and other citizen-centric initiatives that foster sustainable practices and community participation.

The Ministry of MSME, through the successful conduct of Swachhata Pakhwada activities, reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of "Swachh Bharat – Swasth Bharat." The campaign served as a platform to encourage employees, stakeholders and citizens to adopt cleanliness as a way of life, strengthen environmental consciousness and work collectively towards a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

"Swachhata is not merely a campaign; it is a shared responsibility and a lasting commitment towards nation-building."

headline: DELIVERY OF SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL - ‘NIPUN’
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

DELIVERY OF SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL - ‘NIPUN’

30 JUL 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

‘Nipun’ the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV), built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited was delivered to the Indian Navy on 30 Jul 2026 at Visakhapatnam. The vessel has been designed and constructed in accordance with Classification Rules of the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS).

‘Nipun’ draws her name from Sanskrit signifying ‘one who is adept, capable, and well versed in a particular discipline’. True to the name, the ship is highly specialised and is capable of undertaking deep sea dive operations and rescue operations at sea.

The ship is installed with state-of-the-art Dive Equipment and has capability to undertake Deep Sea Saturation Diving. A side diving stage has also been provided for undertaking Diving Operations. The Remotely Operated Vehicles further enhance the ship’s operational capabilities by facilitating diver monitoring and salvage operations. In addition, the ship would also serve as the Mother Ship for the Deep Submergence Rescue Vessel (DSRV), to evacuate personnel in case of an emergency in a submarine.

Nipun’s delivery is yet another milestone in the Indian Navy’s quest for indigenous Shipbuilding upholding the Government’s vision of an ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ with nearly 75 percent Indigenous Content. The delivery marks a major step in bolstering the Indian Navy’s capabilities in the niche domain of Deep Sea Dive Operations.

(Release ID: 2292073)

headline: India Expedites Maritime Capacity Expansion as Government Pushes Viksit Bharat 2047 Goals
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

India Expedites Maritime Capacity Expansion as Government Pushes Viksit Bharat 2047 Goals

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal urges ‘Faster Execution’, calls for 'Speed & Scale' to meet 2030 maritime targets

Govt identifies Port Capacity, Shipbuilding and Digitisation emerge as key Growth Drivers

Port expansion pipeline targets over 700 MTPA of Additional Capacity by 2030

Higher mechanisation, greater private participation to to reshape India's port Ecosystem by 2030

Shipbuilding output surges 41% as New Industrial Clusters position India for Global Manufacturing Growth

30 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

India is accelerating investments across ports, inland waterways and shipbuilding as the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) advances its roadmap towards Viksit Bharat 2047, with a sharp focus on capacity creation, private investment, digitisation and maritime manufacturing.

Chairing a high-level review of the Ministry's Viksit Bharat targets, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping & Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal directed officials to accelerate implementation of flagship projects while maintaining strict adherence to timelines. Sonowal urged officials across the Ministry, major ports and the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) to work with a unified approach to achieve India's long-term maritime ambitions.

The review comes as the Ministry reports significant progress across multiple performance indicators. India has consolidated its position as the world's largest ship recycling nation, while inland waterways cargo has already crossed 200 million tonnes, achieving the Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030 target several years ahead of schedule.

"These achievements demonstrate what India can accomplish when policy, execution and teamwork move together. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the maritime sector has emerged as one of the strongest pillars of India's economic transformation. We must continue to work with the same sense of purpose, uphold the Prime Minister's mantra of ‘Speed and Scale’, and ensure that every milestone under ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ is delivered on time," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Minister also called on officials to strengthen institutional resilience by incorporating lessons from global disruptions into future planning."The evolving geopolitical situation has shown that resilience is as important as growth. Every challenge offers an opportunity to build stronger systems, enhance capacity and prepare India for the future. Our planning must anticipate global uncertainties while keeping India's growth trajectory firmly on course," Sonowal said.

700 MTPA Capacity Addition by 2030

The Ministry is pursuing one of the country's largest maritime infrastructure expansion programmes, targeting more than 700 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of additional port capacity by 2030. Among the flagship projects are the Vadhavan Port, which will add 164 MTPA of capacity by 2030-31, the Tuticorin Outer Harbour project with 39 MTPA, and the Kandla Tuna Tekra Terminal, expected to contribute 33 MTPA by 2027-28.

Overall, the Ministry plans to create an additional 682 MTPA of capacity by 2030 through a combination of new infrastructure, mechanisation and private investment. This includes 306 MTPA at major ports, 193 MTPA at key non-major ports and another 183 MTPA through mechanisation, operational efficiency improvements, public-private partnerships and capacity augmentation at emerging non-major ports.

Mechanisation, PPP to Drive Efficiency

The Ministry aims to increase cargo handling mechanisation across ports from 76% in FY 2025-26 to 93% by 2030, significantly improving operational efficiency and reducing turnaround time. Private sector participation is also expected to expand substantially. Cargo handled through public-private partnership (PPP) projects is projected to rise from 44% in 2013-14 to 85% by 2030-31, reflecting the Government's continued emphasis on private capital and operational expertise in port development. The Ministry has also set a target of achieving 100% digitisation across the maritime sector by 2030, with integrated digital platforms expected to improve logistics efficiency, transparency and service delivery.

Shipbuilding Push Gains Momentum

India's shipbuilding sector also recorded strong momentum during the review period. Domestic shipbuilding output increased 41%, rising from 40,923 gross tonnes (GT) in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025. To support long-term manufacturing growth, the Government has granted in-principle approvals for greenfield shipbuilding clusters in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, each with a planned capacity of 1.2 million GT. Similar approvals for Maharashtra and Odisha are expected by August-September 2026.

A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding has also been signed with HD Hyundai-KSOE for developing a shipbuilding cluster in Tamil Nadu, while extending 100% financial support for common maritime infrastructure required for these industrial ecosystems. The review noted a sharp improvement in the value of vessels being built domestically. The average contract value per vessel has increased more than fivefold to ₹212 crore, compared with ₹41 crore previously, indicating India's growing capability to manufacture larger and technologically advanced ships.

The Union Minister underlined the Ministry's roadmap under Viksit Bharat 2047 to position India among the world's leading maritime economies by strengthening infrastructure, expanding logistics capacity, boosting domestic manufacturing and enhancing global competitiveness.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways announced an accelerated maritime infrastructure expansion plan aiming to add over 700 MTPA of port capacity by 2030, alongside targets for mechanisation, private participation, digitisation and increased shipbuilding output under the Viksit Bharat 2047 agenda.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Target: >700 MTPA additional port capacity by 2030.  
- Flagship projects: Vadhavan Port (164 MTPA by FY 2030‑31), Tuticorin Outer Harbour (39 MTPA), Kandla Tuna Tekra Terminal (33 MTPA by FY 2027‑28).  
- Total planned capacity addition: 682 MTPA by 2030, comprising 306 MTPA at major ports, 193 MTPA at key non‑major ports, and 183 MTPA via mechanisation, PPPs and emerging port development.  
- Mechanisation target: raise cargo handling mechanisation from 76% (FY 2025‑26) to 93% by 2030.  
- Private sector participation: PPP‑handled cargo to grow from 44% (2013‑14) to 85% by FY 2030‑31.  
- Maritime digitisation goal: achieve 100% digitisation across the sector by 2030.  
- Inland waterways cargo exceeded 200 million tonnes, meeting the Maritime India Vision 2030 target ahead of schedule.  
- Shipbuilding output increased 41%, rising from 40,923 GT in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025.  
- Greenfield shipbuilding clusters approved in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat (1.2 million GT each); approvals for Maharashtra and Odisha expected Aug‑Sept 2026.  
- MoU with HD Hyundai‑KSOE for a Tamil Nadu shipbuilding cluster; 100% financial support for common maritime infrastructure.  
- Average contract value per vessel rose >5× to ₹212 crore (from ₹41 crore).
